regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler is the top resort here, with 45" over the window. The big day is Friday, with 19". Rain is the main concern early in the week, and Environment Canada has a special weather statement from Tuesday through Thursday night. Cypress Mountain has 11" total, mostly on Saturday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain leads with 14" total, and Friday brings the biggest day at 6". The NWS expects rain and snow mixing Friday and Friday night, with strong southwest winds at times earlier in the week. Mt. Baker is at 13", with 7" possible on Saturday. Stevens Pass has 9".

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Jay Peak tops the region at 14" over the window, with 8" on Thursday. Whiteface and Stowe are close behind at 11" and 10", both with their biggest day on Thursday. Snow showers and wind are the main story early in the week, with cold temperatures in the 20s overnight Tuesday.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Whitewater is the top resort here at 7", with 3" on Saturday. Revelstoke has 6" total, with 3" expected Saturday. Snow levels sit high at times, so expect rain at lower elevations on Monday and Tuesday. RED Mountain has 4" total.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center expects an atmospheric river to bring more rain and high mountain snow to the West Coast around Sunday Nov 15 into early the following week. Confidence in the exact track and snow levels is moderate.
